params.name: structurePath
params.description: Pathname of 4D structure file to be checked; pass an empty string to show an Open file dialog

params.name: dataPath
params.description: Pathname (or file name) of the 4D data file (.4DD) to check; pass an empty string to show an Open file dialog

params.name: objects
params.description: Which object types to check: sum of Verify Records and/or Verify Indexes bit values, or Verify All

sentinelValues.meaning: Verify all (Verify Records + Verify Indexes plus a full internal check)
Verify indexes: checks physical index consistency only, cannot detect duplicated keys
Equivalent to Verify Records + Verify Indexes (12)

params.name: options
params.description: Verification/log options: sum of applicable bit values

sentinelValues.meaning: Do not create a log file
Timestamp the log file name so it does not replace a previous log file

params.name: method
params.description: Name of a project method called regularly during verification with progress/error/warning events; an empty string or invalid name disables the callback

params.name: tablesArray
params.description: Table numbers whose records to check; if omitted/empty and objects includes Verify Records, all tables are checked

params.name: fieldsArray
params.description: 2D array: for each row, element {0} is a table number and elements {1...x} are indexed field numbers whose indexes to check; if omitted/empty and objects includes Verify Indexes, all indexes are checked

constraints: The designated data file is opened read-only; no other application should access it in write mode during the check, or results may be distorted.

The method callback receives up to 5 params ($messageType, $objectType, $messageText, $table, $reserved) and must return an Integer: 0 continues normally, -128 stops without error, any other value stops and is returned as the error number (interceptable by an error-handling method); execution cannot be interrupted after the End of execution event ($messageType=4).

By default a log file in XML format is written to the database's Logs folder, named after the structure file (e.g. myDB_Verify_Log.xml, or with a timestamp suffix if the Timestamp log file name option is passed); its path is returned in the Document system variable regardless of which options were passed.
To verify the currently open data file instead, use VERIFY CURRENT DATA FILE.
